entries.title: Webinars are generally available, included with CRM
entries.summary: Every organization with **CRM** can now run webinars from **Program → Webinars**: connect Zoom, Goldcast, ON24 or another webinar platform, import or create a webinar, publish it, and get attendance, engagement, the recording, clips and personal recaps back. There is no Early Access request any more.

enable.path: Included with CRM — Program → Webinars

entries.use_case: Customers on CRM run their webinars where their speakers, sessions and contacts already live, and the follow-up (recording, clips, recaps, Advocacy) happens without exporting anything.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on: every CRM organization has Webinars. Tell CRM customers who run webinars that it is there, and point them at Apps → Webinars to connect their platform. Orgs without CRM see a Webinars upsell; that is a CRM conversation.

internal.when_to_bring_up: With any CRM customer that runs webinars on Zoom, Goldcast, ON24, BigMarker, GoTo Webinar, Webex or Microsoft Teams, and in CRM renewals and upsells.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every CRM organization that runs webinars.
internal.staff_path: Program → Webinars (CRM organizations); Apps → Webinars to connect a platform
internal.gotchas: Webinars no longer ride on the Field Events Early Access: an org with Field Events but no CRM loses nothing it used (no customer org was in that state on 2026-11-01). Field Events, Luma, LinkedIn Events and HubSpot stay in Early Access. The Zoom app is still a Draft in the Zoom Marketplace, so connecting Zoom is set up with our team.
internal.talk_track: Webinars come with your CRM: run them on the platform you already use and let Sessionboard handle the follow-up.

entries.title: Webinars: run webinars on ON24, with resources viewed
entries.summary: ON24 is now a webinar platform for **Program → Webinars**: create and update webcasts in ON24, register people, and bring back live attendance, ON24's engagement score, poll answers, Q&A, group chat, reactions, CTA widgets, survey answers and the resources each attendee viewed, plus the archive recording into Media.

enable.path: Included with CRM — Program → Webinars

entries.use_case: Customers who run their webinar program on ON24 get the same loop as Zoom and Goldcast, with ON24's richer engagement data on every contact record.

cs_action.note: Webinars are included with CRM: every CRM organization has Program → Webinars. Connecting the provider app is a per-org step in Apps.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer runs webinars on ON24, especially medical and B2B marketing teams who rely on ON24 engagement scores.
internal.who_should_get_it: ON24 Elite customers.
internal.staff_path: Apps → the provider, then Program → Webinars
internal.gotchas: ON24's API cannot add presenters: speakers are added in ON24 Presentation Manager. ON24 has no personal join link. Orgs on the legacy ON24 import reuse its credentials automatically. Not yet verified against a live ON24 account (time zone codes, archive download auth).
internal.talk_track: Your ON24 webcasts, with every engagement signal ON24 captures, on the contact record.

entries.title: Goldcast webinars: reliable publish, reschedule, registration and attendance
entries.summary: Goldcast webinars now publish, reschedule and sync on Goldcast's documented API only: speakers land on the session, test events show a **Test** badge in the import list, ratings on Goldcast's 1 to 5 scale count toward the Speaker Score, and attendance comes from each registrant's live, on-demand or in-person record.

enable.path: Included with CRM — Program → Webinars

entries.use_case: Goldcast webinars stay in step with Studio, and the attendance and ratings that come back are complete enough to act on.

cs_action.note: Webinars are included with CRM: every CRM organization has Program → Webinars. Connecting the provider app is a per-org step in Apps.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Goldcast customer reports missing attendance or speakers in Studio.
internal.who_should_get_it: Goldcast customers.
internal.staff_path: Apps → the provider, then Program → Webinars
internal.gotchas: Goldcast's session attendance report answers HTML 500, so attendance is read from event members. On the test account Goldcast's documented registration endpoint answered success without adding the registrant; the push now fails honestly and retries. A move that exceeds the account's longest allowed event must be made in Studio.
internal.talk_track: Goldcast and Sessionboard agree on who came and how they rated it.

entries.title: Webinars: walk-ins count, one Dispatch per webinar, nudges every 12 hours at most
entries.summary: People who join a webinar without registering are now added as checked-in registrants, so their attendance and engagement count. Reopening **Share with your team** returns the webinar's existing Dispatch draft, the social pack is written in the background, a teammate is nudged at most once every 12 hours, and a double click never sends or posts twice.

enable.path: Included with CRM — Program → Webinars

where.path: Program → Webinars → a webinar → People and After

entries.use_case: Attendance reports include everyone who showed up, and teammates are reminded without being spammed.

cs_action.note: Webinars are included with CRM: every CRM organization has Program → Webinars. Connecting the provider app is a per-org step in Apps.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why some attendees were missing from a webinar report, or about repeated Dispatch reminders.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any webinar customer.
internal.staff_path: Apps → the provider, then Program → Webinars
internal.gotchas: Walk-ins need an email address from the provider; hosts and presenters are never added. The nudge toast still counts everyone who has not shared, including people inside the 12-hour cooldown who were not emailed. The 'Writing the posts' state needs web-ui-v2 #1393.
internal.talk_track: Everyone who came is counted; nobody gets nagged.

entries.title: Apps: a Webinars category, with every webinar platform open to every organization
entries.summary: **Apps** now has a **Webinars** category holding Zoom Webinars, Goldcast, ON24 and the other webinar platforms, and any organization can connect them without Early Access. Creating and running webinars from **Program → Webinars** is included with CRM.
entries.use_case: Customers find their webinar platform in one place and can connect it straight away, for recordings in Media and webinar history in Speaker CRM.

cs_action.note: Connecting is open to everyone. Running webinars from Program → Webinars comes with CRM: nothing to turn on for CRM customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks which webinar platforms Sessionboard connects to.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organization that runs webinars.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Webinars
internal.gotchas: The Zoom app is still a Draft in the Zoom Marketplace, so only Zoom users on Sessionboard's own account can authorize it until Zoom's review passes. BigMarker, GoTo Webinar, Webex Webinars and Microsoft Teams Webinars cards appear as their own releases ship.
internal.talk_track: Every webinar platform you use, one click away.

entries.title: Attend app sign-in: code first in the subject, resend timer, help-desk codes
entries.summary: The Attend app's sign-in email now leads its subject with the 6-digit code, in the attendee's app language. **Send a new code** waits 60 seconds, **I have a code** takes a code without another email, and a link opened before signing in comes back after. Check-in staff can **Show an app sign-in code** for an attendee whose email never arrived.

where.path: Attend app → sign-in; staff mode → a registration

entries.use_case: Attendees get into the event app faster, and the help desk can sign in someone whose email is stuck in a filter.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports attendees not receiving sign-in emails at the event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every event using the Attend app with email sign-in.
internal.staff_path: Attend app → staff mode (check-in link) → a registration → Show an app sign-in code
internal.gotchas: Needs web-api #5044 in production and the app update from lennd/sessionboard-mobile#132 (EAS preview channel on merge; production is a manual promotion). Desk codes are single use and appear in History → Attendees.
internal.talk_track: Code in the subject, a resend timer, and a help-desk fallback when the email never comes.

entries.title: Webinars: six share cards to post before the webinar
entries.summary: Every webinar now gets six on-brand share cards on its **Overview** tab, with the title, date and time, speakers and a registration QR code. Three show the speakers' faces and three do not. Pick which ones speakers, co-presenters and attendees see on their Advocacy share page, download any of them, or send them to your team as a Dispatch. They retire when the webinar starts.

enable.path: Included with CRM — Program → Webinars

where.path: Program → Webinars → a webinar → Overview → Share cards

entries.use_case: Organizers get promotion assets for every webinar without opening a design tool, and speakers and teammates get a card to post that already carries their tracked registration link.

cs_action.note: Made automatically the first time the webinar's Overview tab is opened; choosing cards for Advocacy needs Advocacy update on the event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to get speakers to promote a webinar, or compares us with InGo, Snöball or Gleanin for registration-driving share cards.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every org running webinars in Sessionboard.
internal.staff_path: Program → Webinars → a webinar → Overview
internal.gotchas: Only public speakers appear on the cards. A speaker without a photo shows as initials on the three face designs. Cards are 1200×627 stills. After the start they leave share pages and new Dispatches use clips. Posting from the share kit uploads the card as a native LinkedIn image.
internal.talk_track: Six cards in your brand, in front of every speaker and registrant, before you have written a single promo post.

entries.title: Webinars: post a webinar as a LinkedIn Event in one click
entries.summary: A webinar's **Overview** now offers **Create LinkedIn Event**. It posts the webinar on your company page with its title, time, description, speakers, cover image and a registration link tagged for LinkedIn, and keeps it up to date until the start. Registrations through LinkedIn land in the webinar with their join link. **Apps → LinkedIn Events** is open to every organization.

enable.path: Apps → Event channels → LinkedIn Events (limited release; ask your Customer Success Manager)

entries.use_case: Marketing teams get each webinar in front of their LinkedIn followers without copying details by hand, and see how many registrations LinkedIn brought in.

cs_action.note: The organization connects LinkedIn Events in Apps as a page admin or content admin; no staff step.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer promotes webinars on LinkedIn or asks where their registrants come from.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organization that runs webinars and has a LinkedIn company page.
internal.staff_path: Apps → LinkedIn Events, then a webinar's Overview
internal.gotchas: Not usable until the LinkedIn Pages app credentials are in production (SB-10701) and LinkedIn approves Community Management Standard Tier; until then only pages run by admins on Sessionboard's developer app can be posted to. LinkedIn does not share its Attend list: registrations come back through the registration page (UTM-tagged) or, when Lead Sync is turned on for the connection, LinkedIn's registration form. The registration choice, organizer page and format cannot change after creation, and LinkedIn locks the event once it starts.
internal.talk_track: Your webinar on LinkedIn in one click, with every sign-up still in Sessionboard.

entries.title: Webinars: speakers and attendees can invite their connections to the LinkedIn Event
entries.summary: When a webinar is posted as a LinkedIn Event, the Advocacy share page, the Dispatch share kit and Dispatch emails now link to it. They ask speakers, teammates and attendees to click **Attend** and use LinkedIn's **Invite** to bring their connections. Posts keep each person's tracked registration link.

enable.path: Apps → Event channels → LinkedIn Events (limited release; ask your Customer Success Manager)

where.path: Advocacy share page, Dispatch share kit and Dispatch emails for a webinar posted as a LinkedIn Event

entries.use_case: LinkedIn lets people who are attending an event invite their 1st-degree connections, and no tool can do it for them. Pointing every speaker at the event turns each speaker's network into invitations, while their posts still credit sign-ups to them.

cs_action.note: Shows by itself once the webinar's LinkedIn Event is posted; nothing to turn on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer posts webinars as LinkedIn Events, or asks how to get speakers to promote beyond a single post.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organization that posts webinars as LinkedIn Events.
internal.staff_path: A webinar's Overview → Channels shows the LinkedIn Event; open a speaker's share link or a Dispatch share kit for the same event
internal.gotchas: Shows only while the LinkedIn Event is posted and the webinar has not ended. LinkedIn does not tell us who clicked Attend or who was invited, so invitations are not counted; registrations from them come in through the registration page like any other LinkedIn sign-up. The Dispatch email line is in English; the speaker-portal Promote page is translated (de, es, fr).
internal.talk_track: Every speaker can invite their whole LinkedIn network to your webinar in two clicks, and you still see who registered because of them.

entries.title: Webinars: share the recording on your LinkedIn page after the webinar
entries.summary: When a webinar was posted as a LinkedIn Event, its **After** tab now has **Share the recording on LinkedIn**. It posts the on-demand link or a clip as a video on the same company page. The text starts from the social pack's LinkedIn post, and you see a preview and confirm before anything goes out.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access

where.path: Program → Webinars → a webinar → After → Share the recording on LinkedIn

entries.use_case: LinkedIn locks an event once it starts, so the recording can't go on the event itself. This puts the replay in front of the same followers in one click, with views tagged as coming from LinkedIn.

cs_action.note: Shows on the After tab once the webinar has ended, if it was posted as a LinkedIn Event. Posting needs integration management, the same as creating the LinkedIn Event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer posts webinars as LinkedIn Events and asks how to promote the recording, or why they can't add the replay to the LinkedIn Event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organization that posts webinars as LinkedIn Events.
internal.staff_path: A webinar's After tab → Share the recording on LinkedIn
internal.gotchas: One post per webinar. Edit or delete it on LinkedIn afterwards. A clip goes up as native video only once it has been cut and rendered in Media, as an MP4 of 200 MB or less. Needs the same LinkedIn Pages app setup as LinkedIn Events (SB-10701).
internal.talk_track: The webinar is over, the LinkedIn Event is locked, and the replay is still one click from your page's feed.

entries.title: Connect GoTo Webinar as a webinar provider
entries.summary: Organizers can now connect a GoTo Webinar account via OAuth and run the full webinar loop: import existing webinars, publish and sync sessions, collect registrants, track attendance, pull Q&A, poll and survey answers, and import recordings into **Media → Discover**. Webhooks keep data current automatically. Chat, reactions, and CTA clicks are not available from GoTo's API.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable GoTo Webinar; then Apps → GoTo Webinar → Connect

entries.use_case: Teams that run webinars on GoTo Webinar can manage the full content lifecycle — planning, publishing, registrant collection, attendance, engagement data, and post-event recordings — without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: Requires GOTO_CLIENT_ID and GOTO_CLIENT_SECRET set in Doppler, plus webhook keys created once with the GoTo developer account. Not yet live-verified against a real GoTo account — coordinate with engineering before enabling for a customer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a prospect or customer runs webinars on GoTo Webinar and wants to manage content, registrants, and post-event assets in Sessionboard.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already using the Webinars feature on Zoom or Goldcast who also run GoTo Webinar events.
internal.staff_path: Apps → GoTo Webinar → Connect
internal.gotchas: GoTo's API registration depends on the customer's GoTo plan (403 if not available). Chat, reactions, and CTA clicks are not supported. Poll/survey answers have no timestamp. The PR has not been verified against a live GoTo account yet.
internal.talk_track: GoTo Webinar is now a supported provider alongside Zoom and Goldcast — connect it once and the full loop (import, sync, registrants, attendance, Q&A, recordings) runs automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The /webinars/overview guide covers Zoom and Goldcast; it should add a section documenting how to connect GoTo Webinar, what data syncs, and the GoTo-specific limitations (no chat/reactions, plan-dependent registration, no stored recording URLs).
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard's webinar integration lets you plan, publish, and follow up on webinars from the same workspace you use to manage speakers and sessions. Connecting a provider means registrant lists, attendance records, Q&A, poll results, and recordings flow back automatically, so your team has a single source of truth for every webinar. Engagement data feeds Pathways and Signals, and recordings land in Media ready to clip, transcribe, or share.

entries.title: Dispatch nudge toast accurately reports who was actually reached
entries.summary: The confirmation toast after nudging teammates to share a Dispatch now counts only the people who were actually sent a message. If everyone was nudged in the last 12 hours, the toast reads "No one nudged" with an explanation instead of a misleading success count. When some people are in the cooldown window, the toast shows how many were reached and how many were skipped, e.g. "Nudged 3 people via Slack + email. Skipped 2 people nudged in the last 12 hours." Channel wording (Slack + email, on Slack, or by email) now reflects the channels actually used.
entries.use_case: Organizers who nudge teammates to share a Dispatch can now trust the confirmation toast — if nobody was actually messaged because everyone is in the 12-hour cooldown window, the toast says so clearly instead of claiming success.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that nudge confirmations seem wrong or that they nudged people but nobody received a message.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org using Dispatch share kits with Slack or email nudging.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Dispatch → [dispatch] → Share Kit → Nudge
internal.gotchas: The fix requires the API to return a coolingDown field (introduced in API PR #5037); older API versions without that field fall back to the previous behaviour.
internal.talk_track: The nudge toast now tells you exactly who was reached and who was skipped due to the 12-hour cooldown, so you are never left wondering whether your nudge actually went out.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the 12-hour nudge cooldown window and explain what the toast messages mean when some or all recipients are cooling down.
draft.why_use_it: Dispatch lets you send a share kit to teammates so they can amplify event content on social channels. The nudge feature reminds people who have not yet shared, and the confirmation toast tells you exactly how many people were reached and through which channels, so you always know the real status of your outreach.

entries.title: Generate a structured session recap from an uploaded recording
entries.summary: Organizers can now upload a recording for any session that wasn't captioned live and get an AI-generated **Recap** — including a summary, takeaways, topics, chapters, quotes, stats, and people — in minutes. Edit or hide individual sections, mark the session **Off the record** to suppress everything, then **Publish** to make the recap available in the Attend app, where **Ask** can quote the transcript.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Session Recaps; then Program → Sessions → [session] → Recap → Attach Recording

entries.use_case: Customers who record sessions but don't run live captions can still give attendees a polished, searchable recap — and let Ask answer questions about what was said — without any manual transcription work.

cs_action.note: Feature is gated behind the 'session-recap' cost feature; CS must enable it per org before organizers see the Recap tab on sessions.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer records sessions but doesn't run live captions, or when they want to extend the value of post-event recordings in the Attend app.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Attend app with Ask enabled, especially those with large recorded-session libraries and no live captioning setup.
internal.staff_path: Program → Sessions → [session] → Recap
internal.gotchas: Only 'recording' or 'audio' media types are accepted — clips and caption-only rows return a 400. Off-record sessions block upload and take down any already-published recap. The recap waits in 'transcribing' status until Deepgram finishes; publishing is not available until generation completes. The transcript is not copied to Session_Transcription_Fragments (and therefore not available to Ask) if the transcript section is hidden at publish time.
internal.talk_track: Upload the recording, get a structured recap in minutes, hide anything sensitive, and publish — attendees can read it in the app and Ask can answer questions about it.

draft.docs_gap: The /marketing/recaps guide should add a section covering the upload-recording path for sessions that weren't captioned live, including the off-record gate, the hidden-sections controls, the publish/unpublish flow, and how the published recap surfaces in the Attend app and feeds Ask.
draft.why_use_it: Recaps turn session recordings into structured, scannable content — summaries, key takeaways, chapter markers, notable quotes, and more — so attendees can revisit what mattered without rewatching the full video. Organizers control exactly what is visible: individual sections can be hidden, sensitive sessions can be marked off the record, and nothing reaches attendees until it is explicitly published. Once published, the Attend app's Ask assistant can draw on the transcript to answer attendee questions about the session.

entries.title: Webinars: run webinars on BigMarker, with full engagement sync
entries.summary: BigMarker is now a supported webinar platform under **Program → Webinars**: connect with an API key in **Apps → BigMarker**, then create and update webinars, add speakers as presenters, register attendees (each gets a personal join link), and pull back live attendance, time in session, engaged time, poll answers, Q&A, chat, reactions, offer clicks, handout downloads, ratings, survey answers and on-demand replay activity. The webinar recording is imported into **Media**, and past BigMarker conferences with recordings appear in **Media → Discover**.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Field Events; then Apps → BigMarker

entries.use_case: Customers who run their webinar program on BigMarker get the same publish-register-sync loop as Zoom and Goldcast, including BigMarker's full engagement data — polls, Q&A, chat, CTAs, surveys and on-demand replays — on every contact record.

cs_action.note: Webinars ride on the Field Events Early Access (gatherings feature). The customer must also have API access enabled on their BigMarker account — BigMarker controls this entitlement; direct them to BigMarker support if the connection returns 'API access is not enabled for this account'.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer runs webinars on BigMarker and wants registration, engagement data or recordings in Sessionboard.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already on the Field Events / Webinars beta who use BigMarker as their webinar platform.
internal.staff_path: Apps → BigMarker, then Program → Webinars
internal.gotchas: BigMarker must enable API access on the customer's account before the connection will succeed (account-level entitlement on BigMarker's side, not a Sessionboard issue). Some BigMarker accounts use a custom base URL (e.g. web.bigmarker.com instead of www.bigmarker.com) — the connection form has an API Base URL field for this. BigMarker has no webhook signature; the connector uses an HMAC URL token instead. Live read paths (registrants, attendance, engagement, recordings) were not verified against a live account before merge — covered by contract tests only.
internal.talk_track: Your BigMarker webinars, with every engagement signal BigMarker captures, on the contact record — same loop as Zoom and Goldcast.

draft.docs_gap: The /apps/bigmarker-integration guide exists in the article index but should document the API Base URL field, the Channel ID option, how the HMAC webhook token works, known BigMarker account entitlement requirements, and the full list of engagement signals that sync back.
draft.why_use_it: BigMarker is a webinar platform built for interactive, marketing-focused events. Connecting it to Sessionboard means every webinar you run on BigMarker is created, updated and kept in sync from one place, with registrations flowing automatically and every engagement signal BigMarker captures — attendance time, poll answers, Q&A, chat, reactions, CTA clicks, survey responses and replay views — written back to the contact record. That data feeds Signals and Pathways so you can act on audience behaviour without leaving Sessionboard.

entries.title: Reach Results: see which channels, sessions and people drove event conversions
entries.summary: A new **Marketing → Measure → Results** section shows how registrations and other conversions are attributed across channels and sessions, using a position-based model (first/last touch each earn 40%, middle touches share 20%). The **Channels** view shows credited conversions and cost-per-conversion per channel; the **Sessions** view shows which sessions drove conversions through shares and clicks; and the **Journey** tab on a contact record shows that person's ordered touch history with credit share. HubSpot contacts also receive four new properties — **sb_first_touch_channel**, **sb_last_touch_channel**, **sb_conversion_count** and **sb_last_conversion_at** — written automatically when Pathways syncs contacts.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Reach; then Marketing → Measure → Results

entries.use_case: Organizers running Advocacy or Dispatch campaigns can see exactly which channels and sessions earned registrations, how much each conversion cost, and the full touch journey for any individual contact — without leaving Sessionboard or exporting to a spreadsheet.

cs_action.note: Reach Results is gated behind feature--reach, which no org has in production yet. CS must enable the flag before any customer can see the Results nav item or the Journey tab. HubSpot write-back also requires an active HubSpot connection with contact properties turned on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to measure ROI across their Advocacy and Dispatch campaigns, or when they want to see which sessions drove the most registrations.
internal.who_should_get_it: Orgs actively using Advocacy or Dispatch who also want channel-level conversion reporting; HubSpot customers on Pathways get the four contact properties automatically once the flag is on.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Measure → Results (only visible with feature--reach enabled)
internal.gotchas: Ad spend and impressions (REACH-006) and pixel page views (REACH-002) are not yet wired in, so spend_cents is always 0 and cost-per-conversion is null until those ship. Signals data is keyed by attendee, not person, so it does not feed the touch loader yet. HubSpot timeline events per conversion are deferred. A page of more than 50,000 conversions returns null and no Reach properties are written for that page.
internal.talk_track: Reach Results shows you which channels and sessions earned each registration, with a full touch journey on every contact record — and it writes first/last touch channel and conversion count straight into HubSpot.

draft.docs_gap: The article index has no dedicated Reach / Results guide; the closest is the Marketing overview. A new guide covering the Results page, the attribution model, the Channels and Sessions views, the Journey tab, and the HubSpot property write-back should be created under /marketing/reach-results.
draft.why_use_it: Reach Results answers the question every event marketer faces after a campaign: which channels actually drove registrations, and which sessions made people act? The attribution engine assigns credit across every touch a person had — Advocacy shares, Dispatch clicks, campaign emails and direct visits — so you can compare channels on equal footing and identify the content that converts. The Journey tab on each contact record shows the exact sequence of touches that led to a conversion, giving your team the context to have better follow-up conversations.

entries.title: CfP co-author "This is me" refusal now appears under the correct row
entries.summary: When a co-author row is marked **This is me** and the account's profile email does not match, the validation message **"The participant marked 'This is me' must use the email on your profile…"** now appears inline under that row's email field, in addition to the toast notification. Previously it appeared only as a toast, making it unclear which row caused the error.

where.path: Call for Papers submission form → co-author row → This is me

entries.use_case: Submitters who mark a co-author row as "This is me" with a mismatched email now see the error directly under the offending field, so they know exactly what to fix without guessing which row triggered the toast.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Only if a customer reports confusion about the 'This is me' email validation on CfP submission forms.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event using a Call for Papers form with co-author rows.
internal.staff_path: Call for Papers submission form → co-author section → This is me toggle
internal.gotchas: The fix matches two distinct refusal messages (a Set): the original 'already associated with another account' message and the new profile-email mismatch message. Both now pin to the row.

draft.docs_gap: The submission forms guide should note that the "This is me" co-author field validates against the signed-in user's profile email and surfaces errors inline on the row.

entries.title: Connect Microsoft Teams Webinars and Town Halls as a webinar provider
entries.summary: Organizers can now connect **Microsoft Teams Webinars** (including Town Halls) as a webinar provider under **Apps → Webinars**. After connecting with a Microsoft 365 account, Sessionboard imports webinars and town halls the user organizes or co-organizes, syncs registrants, attendance records, engagement data, and session recordings back into the platform, and pushes Sessionboard registrants to Teams. A Microsoft 365 tenant admin must grant admin consent before any user in that tenant can connect.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Microsoft Teams Webinars; then Apps → Webinars → Connect → Microsoft Teams Webinars

entries.use_case: Organizations that run webinars or town halls on Microsoft Teams can manage the full lifecycle — publishing, registration, attendance, engagement and recordings — without leaving Sessionboard. Registrants added in Sessionboard are pushed to Teams automatically, and anyone who registers directly on the Teams page is captured from attendance records.

cs_action.note: The Microsoft Entra app exists and secrets are in Doppler for all regions, but the publisher is not yet verified (no MPN ID). A customer's Microsoft 365 tenant admin must grant admin consent before any user in that tenant can connect — Microsoft shows 'Need admin approval' otherwise. Recordings require the OnlineMeetings.Read permission to be added to the Entra app and the connection to be re-made. Confirm both prerequisites are met before pointing a customer at this.

internal.when_to_bring_up: With any CRM customer that runs webinars or town halls on Microsoft Teams, and in CRM renewals or upsells where the customer is a Microsoft 365 shop.
internal.who_should_get_it: CRM organizations whose webinar platform is Microsoft Teams Webinars or Teams Town Halls.
internal.staff_path: Program → Webinars; Apps → Webinars → Connect → Microsoft Teams Webinars
internal.gotchas: Tenant admin consent is required before any user in a customer's Microsoft 365 tenant can connect — without it Microsoft blocks the OAuth flow with 'Need admin approval'. Recordings are unavailable until OnlineMeetings.Read is added to the Sessionboard Entra app and the customer reconnects. Teams emails registrants its own join link; Sessionboard's confirmation email still goes but contains no personal join link. Teams-page registrants who bypass the Sessionboard registration flow are recovered from attendance records after the webinar ends, not in real time.
internal.talk_track: If your webinars run on Microsoft Teams, Sessionboard now connects directly: publish from here, get attendance and recordings back automatically, and feed your post-event follow-up without any manual exports.

draft.docs_gap: The guide at /apps/microsoft-teams-webinars-integration should document the tenant admin consent requirement (and what the user sees if consent has not been granted), the OnlineMeetings.Read prerequisite for recordings, the fact that Teams emails its own join link so Sessionboard's confirmation carries no personal join URL, and how Teams-page registrants are recovered from attendance records after the event.
draft.why_use_it: Microsoft Teams Webinars connects your Teams webinars and town halls to the same speaker, session and contact data you already manage in Sessionboard. Attendance, engagement signals, and session recordings flow back automatically so your follow-up — clips, recaps, Advocacy campaigns — starts the moment a webinar ends. Running everything from one place means no manual exports and no data living in a separate platform.

entries.title: Microsoft Teams channels and people available across notifications, Dispatch, Learning, webinars and workflows
entries.summary: Organizations with Microsoft Teams connected can now route activity through Teams alongside Slack. A **Microsoft Teams** column appears in notification preferences, **Microsoft Teams channels / people** pickers appear in the Dispatch wizard and in Registration notification rules, Learning's **Assign** dialog can announce a course in a Teams channel, the Webinars one-click Dispatch gains a **Microsoft Teams** button, and a `post_teams` action is available in the workflow catalog. The **Apps → Microsoft Teams** page shows connected people and channel counts and a **Download the Teams app package** button.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Microsoft Teams; then Apps → Microsoft Teams

where.path: Apps → Microsoft Teams; Notifications → Preferences; Dispatch wizard; Registration → Notifications; Learning → Assign; Program → Webinars; Automations

entries.use_case: Teams-first organizations can receive Sessionboard notifications, send Dispatch messages, announce learning assignments, and trigger workflow actions directly in Microsoft Teams channels and DMs — without switching to Slack or email.

cs_action.note: The Microsoft Entra app exists and secrets are in Doppler, but the publisher is not yet verified (no MPN ID). A customer's Microsoft 365 admin must grant admin consent before any users in their tenant can connect — Microsoft shows 'Need admin approval' until they do. The Teams app package button is live for connected orgs. The Apps → Microsoft Teams tile is still marked Coming Soon (PRELAUNCH_APP_IDS) until the Entra app and bot are fully ready; do not proactively surface this to customers yet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about Slack alternatives or is a Microsoft 365 / Teams-first shop that wants Sessionboard alerts and Dispatch in Teams.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations that run on Microsoft Teams and want notification routing, Dispatch sends, or workflow actions delivered there instead of or alongside Slack.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Microsoft Teams (org level)
internal.gotchas: Publisher verification (MPN ID) is not yet complete, so tenants that require verified publishers or that restrict user consent will see 'Need admin approval'. The *.ReadWrite.All and Recording.Read.All Graph permissions always require admin consent regardless of verification status. The API PR (web-api #5038) must be in a prod release before any Teams controls appear — they are gated on the API reporting Teams as connected.
internal.talk_track: If your team lives in Microsoft Teams, you can now get Sessionboard notifications, Dispatch messages, learning announcements and workflow posts delivered straight to your Teams channels — the same way Slack works today.

draft.docs_gap: The /integrations/slack guide covers Slack only; a parallel /integrations/microsoft-teams guide should document connecting Teams (admin consent flow, Entra app, publisher verification caveat), notification preferences, Dispatch recipient pickers, Learning announce, webinar Dispatch button, workflow post_teams action, and the Teams app package download.
draft.why_use_it: Connecting Microsoft Teams lets your team receive Sessionboard activity — submission alerts, Dispatch sends, learning announcements and workflow actions — in the channels where they already work. You choose which notification types go to Teams, pick specific channels or people as Dispatch recipients, and announce course assignments to a Teams channel, all from the same surfaces that control Slack today.

entries.title: BigMarker is now a supported webinar platform
entries.summary: **Apps → BigMarker** is now a live connect card (Early Access). Paste an API key — and optionally a Channel ID — to connect BigMarker alongside other webinar providers. Once connected, BigMarker appears in the new-webinar picker, **Webinars → Start**, **Import from provider**, and the event's provider status card. The **Engagement** report gains an **On-demand views** tile when BigMarker reports replay attendees, and a contact's interaction list shows their individual replay.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Field Events; then Apps → BigMarker → Connect

entries.use_case: Teams that run webinars on BigMarker can now connect it directly in Sessionboard, import their webinars, and see live and on-demand engagement — including replay counts per contact — without leaving the platform.

cs_action.note: BigMarker is behind the Field Events Early Access (gatherings). The customer must join Early Access first; then they connect via Apps → BigMarker with their own API key. No staff action is needed to provision the connection itself.

internal.when_to_bring_up: With any customer that runs webinars on BigMarker and is already on CRM or asking about webinar platform support.
internal.who_should_get_it: CRM customers who use BigMarker as their webinar platform.
internal.staff_path: Apps → BigMarker (after Early Access is on)
internal.gotchas: BigMarker only appears in the webinar picker and import dialog once the API confirms it is in the org's offered providers — it will not show up for orgs whose API response does not include BigMarker. On-demand replay interactions have no timeline position, so they never appear on the recording timeline. Handout downloads use the Resources kind from a companion PR (#1395).
internal.talk_track: If you run webinars on BigMarker, you can now connect it in Sessionboard the same way you would Zoom or Goldcast — import your webinars, track live and on-demand engagement, and feed that data into your follow-up workflows.

draft.docs_gap: The /apps/bigmarker-integration guide should document the API key and optional Channel ID fields, the on-demand views tile in the Engagement report, and the fact that replay interactions do not appear on the recording timeline.
draft.why_use_it: The BigMarker integration brings your webinar data — registrations, live attendance, engagement and on-demand replays — into the same place you manage speakers, sessions and follow-up content. Connect once and Sessionboard keeps the data in sync, so you can act on who watched, who replayed and who has not yet engaged, all from the Webinars module.

entries.title: CFP "This is me" row can no longer overwrite an existing contact link
entries.summary: When submitting a proposal, marking a co-author or any row other than your own profile email as **"This is me"** now returns a clear error — **"The participant marked 'This is me' must use the email on your profile…"** — and blocks the submission. Earlier abstracts, portal access, and the contact link are left untouched. First-time submitters are unaffected.

where.path: Submission form → participant list → This is me

entries.use_case: Submitters who have existing abstracts on file can safely add co-authors to a proposal without risking their contact link being moved to a co-author's record, which would hide their earlier submissions and lock them out of future submissions.

cs_action.note: Approximately 50 contact links were moved incorrectly in production between Oct 31 and Nov 1 (AUA 2027 event). A separate data-repair script is being run by engineering. Reach out to affected customers proactively — look for events with a Nov 2 CFP deadline where submitters reported missing abstracts or 'already associated with another account' errors.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports missing abstracts, a wrong email on a speaker profile, or 'already associated with another account' errors after a CFP submission.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running an active CFP where submitters add co-authors on the submission form.
internal.staff_path: Submission form → participant list → This is me (portal view)
internal.gotchas: The data repair for the ~50 moved links from Oct 31–Nov 1 is a separate engineering script and is not part of this fix. First-time submitters (no existing contact link on the event) are unaffected and still create a new link on submit.
internal.talk_track: A bug introduced Oct 31 could silently move a submitter's contact link to a co-author's record when they marked the wrong 'This is me' row. This fix blocks that action with a clear error message and leaves all existing data intact.

draft.docs_gap: The submission-forms guide should note that the "This is me" row must match the submitter's profile email, and explain the error message a submitter sees if they mark a different participant row.
draft.why_use_it: null

entries.title: Microsoft Teams app: Ask Sessionboard, notifications, Dispatch, registration alerts, Learning and workflows
entries.summary: The **Microsoft Teams** app (Apps → Microsoft Teams) now reaches full parity with the Slack integration. Organizers can connect their Microsoft 365 tenant and then: receive event notifications and workflow messages in Teams channels; send **Dispatch** campaigns to Teams users and channels; route registration alerts to Teams channels; deliver Learning assignment and certification messages via Teams; and ask **Ask Sessionboard** questions in a 1:1 chat or by @-mentioning the bot in a channel.

enable.path: Apps → Microsoft Teams → Connect

entries.use_case: Organizations that run on Microsoft Teams can receive Sessionboard notifications, send Dispatch campaigns, and get Learning and registration alerts directly in Teams channels — without switching to Slack or relying on email. Team members can also ask the Sessionboard bot questions in Teams the same way they do in Slack.

cs_action.note: The Azure Bot does not exist yet at merge time. Before pointing any customer at this feature, confirm with engineering that the Azure Bot has been created, the app package has been installed in a test tenant, inbound JWT verification works, installs are recorded, and proactive messages (personal and channel) are delivered. Also note: a customer's Microsoft 365 admin must grant admin consent before any user in their tenant can connect, because the publisher is not yet verified (no MPN ID). The connect card copy explains this, but CSMs should set expectations upfront.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about Slack parity, uses Microsoft Teams as their primary collaboration tool, or wants notifications and Dispatch delivery beyond email.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organization that uses Microsoft Teams and wants Sessionboard notifications, Dispatch, registration alerts, Learning messages or Ask Sessionboard in Teams.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Microsoft Teams
internal.gotchas: 1) Azure Bot must be created before rollout — bot-side features (installs, proactive messages, @mention Q&A) are not live until then. 2) Customer's M365 admin must grant admin consent; users without admin approval see 'Need admin approval' from Microsoft. 3) If the first connect call fails to capture the tenant ID, the connection saves as active but Teams delivery, channel pickers and conversation claims all report it as not connected (SB-10945 open). 4) Large registration digests are split at 24 KiB to stay under Teams' ~28 KB bot-message limit. 5) The UI PR (sessionboard-web-ui-v2 feature/teams-app-ui) must ship alongside this API PR.
internal.talk_track: If your team runs on Microsoft Teams, you can now get Sessionboard notifications, send Dispatch campaigns and ask the Sessionboard bot questions right inside Teams — the same experience Slack users have had.

draft.docs_gap: The article index has no dedicated Microsoft Teams integration guide; a new guide at /integrations/microsoft-teams should document connecting the app, granting admin consent, the bot installation flow, channel pickers, notification routing, Dispatch to Teams recipients, registration alert channels, Learning messages and Ask Sessionboard in Teams — mirroring the structure of /integrations/slack.
draft.why_use_it: Connecting Microsoft Teams brings Sessionboard's notifications, messaging and AI assistant into the collaboration tool your team already lives in. Notifications about submissions, registrations and Learning assignments arrive in the channels you choose, Dispatch campaigns reach Teams users and channels alongside email, and anyone on the team can ask the Sessionboard bot questions in a 1:1 chat or a shared channel without leaving Teams.

entries.title: See how people found your event and trace each registration's journey (Reach Results)
entries.summary: A new **Marketing → Measure → Results** page shows three tables: how people found the event (channel, spend, registrations, cost each), which sessions sold tickets, and a step-by-step journey for each registration. Clicking **Open <name>** on any journey row opens the contact sidebar on a new **Journey** tab, where every touch and its share of the credit is listed in order.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Reach; then Marketing → Measure → Results

where.path: Marketing → Measure → Results; contact sidebar → Journey tab

entries.use_case: Organizers can see which marketing channels drove registrations, which sessions converted attendees, and exactly which touches led a specific person to register — all without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: Reach requires the org-level 'reach' feature flag AND staff (superuser) access. The nav item comes from the API layout config (featureId: reach, superUserOnly). Spend and cost-each columns show $0 until ad-spend data is connected. The UI is safe to ship before the matching API is live — a 403/404 from an older API renders nothing and fires no follow-up calls.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When talking to organizers who want to attribute registrations to marketing channels or understand which sessions drove ticket sales.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations with the Reach feature enabled and staff access; currently limited to superusers.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Measure → Results (org level); contact sidebar → Journey tab
internal.gotchas: The Journey tab on the contact profile only appears when the org has the 'reach' feature flag (hasReach context). Spend and cost-each columns display $0 until ad-spend data is wired up. The page has not yet been clicked through against a live API — only tested against mocks.
internal.talk_track: With Reach Results you can see exactly which channels and sessions drove registrations, and open any contact to trace their full path from first touch to sign-up.

draft.docs_gap: The article index has no dedicated Reach or Results guide; the closest is the Marketing overview. A new guide covering the Results page (channel table, sessions table, journey timeline) and the contact Journey tab should be created.
draft.why_use_it: Reach Results shows you where your registrations actually came from: which channels, which sessions, and which sequence of touches moved each person from first contact to registration. Use it to understand what is working, where budget is going, and how to focus your marketing for the next event. The Journey tab on a contact profile lets you trace one person's full path to registration, touch by touch, with each touch's share of the credit shown in plain language.

entries.title: CFP Review step flags who is marked "This is me" before you submit
entries.summary: The **Review** step of a Call for Proposals submission form now shows a clear identity callout above the **Submit** button. If the signed-in submitter's row is correctly marked, a green **"Submitting as you: Name (email)"** note appears with a **"Not you? Change it."** link. If a different participant's row is marked, an amber **"Is this really you?"** warning names both emails and offers a **"Go to that participant"** button that navigates back to the **Participants** step and scrolls to the mismatched row. If no row is marked, a neutral note with an **"Edit participants"** link appears. Each marked row also shows a **"This is you"** pill — amber with **"Marked as you · different email"** on a mismatch — in both the participants list and linked presentation rows. The callout is shown only to signed-in users on forms that include a participants step.
entries.use_case: Submitters who accidentally mark a co-author's row as "This is me" are warned before they hit Submit, so they can fix the mistake without losing their draft or getting a confusing API error after submission.

cs_action.note: Ships on by default for all events with a participants step in their CFP form. No configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that submitters are confused about which participant row to mark as themselves, or when abstracts are disappearing from a submitter's portal after submission.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event using a CFP submission form with a participants step where submitters add co-authors.
internal.staff_path: Submission form → Review step (visible to signed-in submitters only)
internal.gotchas: The callout does not appear for anonymous or magic-link-only (signed-out) submissions. It also requires the form to have a participants step; forms without one show nothing.
internal.talk_track: Submitters now see a clear green or amber identity check on the Review step before they submit, so co-author mix-ups are caught in the form rather than after the fact.

draft.docs_gap: The submission-forms guide should document the "This is me" participant marking behaviour and the new Review-step identity callout, including what each state (match, mismatch, none) looks like and how to navigate back to fix it.
draft.why_use_it: Session submission forms let submitters identify which participant row represents them, so the platform can attribute the submission correctly. The Review step surfaces this identity check — along with a clear path to correct it — before the form is sent, preventing mismatches that would otherwise cause submissions to fail or disappear from the submitter's portal.

entries.title: Generate sized ad creatives from sessions, get speaker approval, and respect embargoes
entries.summary: Marketers can now create ad creatives from session clips, speaker cards, or pull quotes and automatically generate sized assets for LinkedIn (1:1 and 1.91:1), Meta feed (4:5) and Meta story (9:16) placements under **Marketing → Source & produce → Ad creative**. Each creative moves through a built-in approval chain — marketer → speaker → optional compliance — and the speaker approves (or requests changes) from their own **Creator console** under **Promote → Ad Approvals**. An embargo inherited from the Content Gallery or set manually blocks the creative from being marked usable until the hold lifts.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Reach

entries.use_case: Event marketing teams can turn approved session content into correctly sized social and display ads without leaving Sessionboard, and speakers retain a formal approval step before any creative goes live — reducing legal and brand risk.

cs_action.note: The feature is behind the org Early Access flag 'reach' (staff-only superUserOnly nav). Customers cannot self-serve into it without staff enabling the flag first.

internal.when_to_bring_up: With marketing-forward customers who produce post-event social content from session recordings or speaker cards, especially those with compliance or speaker-approval requirements.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations already using Clips, Quotes or Advocacy who want a structured workflow to produce and approve paid social creatives.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Source & produce → Ad creative (/org/:orgId/media/ad-creative); speaker side at Creator console → Promote → Ad Approvals
internal.gotchas: Display 300×250 and 728×90 and the Meta story 9:16 card format are unsupported in this release — they appear as rows with an 'unsupported' reason. The speaker approval step only works if the speaker has an active Advocacy campaign in the org; without one there is no Creator console to approve from. Compliance step only appears when an embargo applies. The nav item is superUserOnly and does not appear in the customer nav manifest.
internal.talk_track: Reach turns your session content into sized, approved social ads — clips and speaker cards go straight from the program into LinkedIn and Meta placements, with the speaker signing off before anything goes live.

draft.docs_gap: No guide currently covers the Reach Ad Creative workflow, placement catalog, approval chain, or embargo behaviour; a new article under /marketing/ should document the end-to-end flow from creating a creative to marking it usable.
draft.why_use_it: Ad creative lets you build social-ready assets directly from the sessions, clips, speaker cards and pull quotes already in Sessionboard. Each creative is automatically rendered at the right dimensions for LinkedIn, Meta feed and Meta story placements, routed through a marketer-and-speaker approval chain, and held until any content embargo lifts — so every ad that reaches your audience is approved, on-brand and cleared for release.

entries.title: Connect Webex Webinars to run the full webinar loop
entries.summary: Webex Webinars is now a supported webinar platform. Connect a Webex account under **Apps** to create and publish webinars, push registrants, pull attendance with minutes, collect survey ratings, import MP4 recordings into **Media**, and generate recaps and Dispatch sends — the same loop available for Zoom and Goldcast. Account-wide recordings also appear in **Media → Discover** with a **Webex** source for manual import.

enable.path: Apps → Webex → Connect

entries.use_case: Organizations that run webinars on Webex can manage the full lifecycle — registration, live event, attendance, recordings and follow-up — without leaving Sessionboard. Recordings flow automatically into Media so clips, recaps and Dispatch sends are ready as soon as the webinar ends.

cs_action.note: WEBEX_CLIENT_ID and WEBEX_CLIENT_SECRET must be set in Doppler for each environment before any customer can connect. The connecting user also needs a Webex Webinars license on their Cisco account — a standard Webex Meetings account cannot host webinars and will see an error on publish.

internal.when_to_bring_up: With any CRM customer that runs webinars on Cisco Webex, and in CRM renewals where Zoom or Goldcast are not the customer's platform of choice.
internal.who_should_get_it: CRM organizations whose webinar platform is Webex.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Webex → Connect; Program → Webinars; Media → Discover → Webex
internal.gotchas: Chat, polls and Q&A require Webex compliance-officer access (enabled by Cisco on request); without it those signals are absent. Personal join links expire within 60 minutes so registrants receive the webinar's public webLink instead. ARF recordings are skipped; only MP4s appear in Media. Account-wide recordings in Discover include private meeting recordings unrelated to any event — nothing is auto-imported. Media → Discover's Webex source requires org-wide media access; event-only staff and portfolio-scoped members see a 403. The UI half of this feature ships separately in web-ui-v2#1383.
internal.talk_track: If your team runs webinars on Webex, Sessionboard now handles the whole loop: connect once, and registration, attendance, recordings and follow-up all come back automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the six required OAuth scopes, the Webex Webinars license requirement for the connecting user, the compliance-officer access needed for chat/polls/Q&A, the 180-day window for account-wide recordings in Discover, and the org-wide media access requirement for the Discover Webex source.
draft.why_use_it: Webex Webinars connects your Cisco-hosted webinars to the same workflow Sessionboard provides for Zoom and Goldcast: publish the webinar, sync registrants, capture attendance and survey results, and bring the recording back as a Media asset ready for clips, recaps and Dispatch. The connecting user needs a Webex Webinars license on their Cisco account. Chat, polls and Q&A data require Webex compliance-officer access, which Cisco enables on request.

entries.title: Create and approve ad creatives in Reach, with speaker sign-off in the Creator console
entries.summary: A new **Media → Ad Creative** page lets staff create ads from finished clips, saved quotes, or speaker cards, then track each ad through a four-step approval chain (Made → Marketer → Speaker → Compliance). Speakers see a **Speaker Ad Approvals** card in their Creator console where they can approve or request changes on any ad waiting for their sign-off. An **Ad creative** filter option is also available in the audit **History** log.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Reach; then Media → Ad Creative

entries.use_case: Marketing teams that need speaker sign-off before running paid ads can create an ad from existing content, assign the speaker as an approver, and let the speaker approve or request changes directly from their Creator console — without any back-and-forth outside the platform.

cs_action.note: Gated on the 'reach' feature flag AND the useSuperUser() check. Both the API (sessionboard-web-api#5059) and the UI must be deployed before this is visible. Do not surface to customers until both are live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When talking to customers who run paid social or display ads featuring speakers and need a compliant approval workflow before launch.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations with the Reach add-on that produce speaker-driven ad content and need documented speaker consent or compliance sign-off.
internal.staff_path: Media → Ad Creative (org-level, staff/super-user only until GA)
internal.gotchas: The page renders nothing on a 403 or 404, so it is safe to deploy before the API cut. The nav item is staff-only and does not appear in the customer nav manifest. Speaker notification emails are deferred (not in this PR).
internal.talk_track: With Reach Ad Creative, you build the ad from content you already have in Sessionboard, route it through your approval chain — including the speaker — and track every placement's render status and run-readiness in one place.

draft.docs_gap: The Media library guide should add a section covering Ad Creative: how to create an ad from a clip, quote, or speaker card; the four-step approval chain; speaker approval in the Creator console; placement previews; hold dates; and the Ad creative filter in History.
draft.why_use_it: Ad Creative gives you a single place to turn your session clips, pull quotes, and speaker cards into ready-to-run ads. Each ad moves through a structured approval chain — marketer, speaker, and compliance — so every stakeholder signs off before the ad goes live. Placement previews, hold dates, and embargo-aware status messages keep the whole team aligned on what is ready and what is waiting.

entries.title: Exhibitor teams can send their scanned leads directly to their own HubSpot
entries.summary: Sponsor and exhibitor teams using the Attend app can now connect their own HubSpot portal and push scanned leads there automatically. Each lead shows a sync status (**Sent**, **Failed**, **Skipped**), and teams can use **Send to HubSpot** per lead or **Retry** on failures. Auto-send triggers on every scan and edit when enabled.

enable.path: In the Attend app: team lead retrieval settings → Connect HubSpot (OAuth). Requires the Sessionboard Lead Retrieval HubSpot app to be configured by Sessionboard — contact Sessionboard Support to confirm availability.

where.path: Attend app → Lead Retrieval → team settings → HubSpot

entries.use_case: Exhibitor teams that use HubSpot as their CRM can have every badge scan flow into their own HubSpot contacts automatically, eliminating the manual export-and-import step after the event. Teams with mixed email consent are handled safely: leads without a visible email are skipped rather than creating a blank contact.

cs_action.note: A new HubSpot public app ('Sessionboard Lead Retrieval') must be created and its client ID and secret added to Doppler for each region (prod-us, prod-eu, prod-me, dev) before any exhibitor can connect. Until those env vars are set, all new routes return 404 and no CRM key appears in the app — existing lead retrieval is unaffected.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When talking to customers who run exhibit halls and whose exhibitors use HubSpot; especially relevant at renewal or when exhibitors ask about post-event lead follow-up.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with exhibitor or sponsor teams that use HubSpot CRM and have lead retrieval (Attend app) enabled.
internal.staff_path: Attend app → Lead Retrieval → team HubSpot settings
internal.gotchas: The feature is fully off until Sessionboard Support creates the dedicated HubSpot public app and sets ATTEND_LEADS_HUBSPOT_CLIENT_ID and ATTEND_LEADS_HUBSPOT_CLIENT_SECRET in Doppler for each region. The existing org-level HubSpot app cannot be reused. Leads without a visible attendee email are skipped (status: skipped/no_email) — no contact is created. Activity (session check-ins etc.) only flows to HubSpot when the attendee has shared it. Tokens are AES-GCM encrypted at rest.
internal.talk_track: Your exhibitors can now connect their own HubSpot and have every badge scan land as a contact automatically — no CSV export, no manual import, and each team's data stays in their own portal.

draft.docs_gap: The /attend/leads guide should add a section explaining how exhibitor teams connect their own HubSpot, the auto-send and per-lead send options, lead sync statuses (Sent, Failed, Skipped), Retry behaviour, and the privacy rules around email consent and activity sharing.
draft.why_use_it: Lead retrieval in the Attend app lets exhibitor and sponsor teams scan attendee badges and collect contact details on the show floor. Connecting a team's own HubSpot portal means scanned leads appear as HubSpot contacts the moment a badge is scanned, with a note capturing the interaction — so follow-up starts before the event ends. Each team manages its own connection independently, and the organizer's data never crosses into a team's CRM.

entries.title: Organizer-defined networking goals power goal-based attendee suggestions with Skip
entries.summary: Organizers can now define up to six **Networking Goals** (e.g. "Find a vendor", "Meet a buyer") in **Attend → Networking** settings, each with match rules tied to registrant types, registration answers, or exhibitor categories. Attendees are prompted with **"What are you here for?"** on first open, choose up to two goals, and immediately see a **People to Meet** feed matched to those goals — or to goals inferred from their registration. Each suggestion card shows why the person is a match, and attendees can **Skip** a card to hide it for the rest of the day.

enable.path: Attend → Networking → Goals — add at least one goal, then ensure People to Meet and the attendee directory are on

where.path: Attend → Networking (organizer settings); People to Meet tab in the Attend mobile app (attendees)

entries.use_case: Organizers running buyer–seller or community events can define goals like "Find an EHR vendor" or "Meet a potential hire," then let the app surface the right people from the first tap — without requiring attendees to manually fill out a full profile. Attendees who skip the goal prompt still get suggestions inferred from their registration type or answers.

cs_action.note: Goals are off by default — nothing shows until the organizer creates at least one goal AND People to Meet + the directory are both on. CS should walk organizers through defining goals and their match rules before the event opens.

internal.when_to_bring_up: With any Attend customer running a conference where buyer–seller matching, job-fair networking, or community introductions matter — especially when they ask why attendees aren't connecting.
internal.who_should_get_it: Attend customers with People to Meet enabled who have distinct attendee types (buyers/sellers, job-seekers/recruiters, practitioners/vendors).
internal.staff_path: Attend → Networking → Goals (admin); People to Meet in the mobile app (attendee)
internal.gotchas: Goals require People to Meet AND the attendee directory to be on; if either is off, goals are hidden and the API returns goals_off. Attendees must be listed in the directory to appear in or receive suggestions — hidden or withdrawn attendees are excluded. Only goals an attendee explicitly picks are ever shown to others (inferred goals are private). The preview endpoint (Attend → Networking → Goals → Preview) lets organizers test suggestions against real attendees before launch. Skip hides a card for the rest of the event-local day only; it resets the next day.
internal.talk_track: With Networking Goals, you define what each attendee type is here to do, and the app makes the right introductions automatically — no manual profile setup required from attendees.

draft.docs_gap: The /attend/networking guide should add a section covering how to create and configure Networking Goals (label, emoji, match rules by registrant type / registration field / exhibitor category, counterpart goals), how attendee goal selection and inference work, how the People to Meet feed ranks and reasons suggestions, and how to use the goal preview tool.
draft.why_use_it: Networking Goals let you tell the app what different attendee types are trying to accomplish, so it can make warm, relevant introductions from the moment someone opens the app. Attendees who pick a goal see people who fit that goal's rules; people whose registration already signals a goal get suggestions automatically. Match reasons name the goal — never a private registration answer — so every suggestion feels helpful rather than intrusive.

entries.title: Define networking goals and preview attendee matches in the Attend app
entries.summary: A new **Networking goals** card in **Attend → Networking** lets organizers create up to six goals (name, emoji, and matching rules based on registrant types, registration answers, exhibitor categories, or other goals). A **Preview as an attendee** card lets organizers pick one or two goals and see exactly which people and exhibitors the app would recommend — including the reason wording attendees will read — before the event goes live.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Networking Goals; then Attend → Networking

entries.use_case: Organizers running events where attendees come with specific business objectives — such as finding a vendor, raising funding, or hiring — can define those goals and control who the app surfaces as a match for each one. The preview tool lets them verify the recommendations look right before attendees ever open the app.

cs_action.note: Feature is gated behind both the web-api flag (settings.goals array) and a super-user check; it will not appear for standard organizer accounts until both the API release is cut and the flag is enabled for the org. Confirm with engineering before promising availability to a customer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When talking to organizers who run networking-heavy events (investor summits, trade shows, hiring events) and are frustrated that the app only matches on interest tags.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events where attendees have distinct, named business objectives and where the organizer wants to control who gets recommended to whom — especially events with exhibitors or multiple registrant types.
internal.staff_path: Attend → Networking (Networking goals card and Preview as an attendee card)
internal.gotchas: Both cards render only when the API returns settings.goals as an array (requires the companion web-api release) and only for super users. Standard organizer accounts will not see the cards until the feature is fully enabled for their org.
internal.talk_track: Instead of matching attendees only on interest tags, you can now tell the app what attendees are actually trying to accomplish — 'find an EHR vendor', 'meet seed-stage investors' — and set the rules for who qualifies as a match. Then preview it yourself before anyone else sees it.

draft.docs_gap: The /attend/networking guide should add a section covering how to create and configure networking goals (name, emoji, matching rules) and how to use the Preview as an attendee tool to validate recommendations before the event.
draft.why_use_it: Attendee networking in the Attend app goes beyond shared interests when you define goals: each goal describes why someone is at the event and who they should meet. The app uses those rules to surface the right people and exhibitors with a clear reason, so attendees spend less time searching and more time in valuable conversations. The preview lets you walk through the experience as an attendee — choosing goals and seeing the exact recommendations and reason text — before the event opens.

entries.title: Control the "This is me" submitter row per submission form
entries.summary: A new per-form toggle, **Enable "This is me"** (off by default on all existing forms), controls whether the CfP submission form marks one participant row as the submitter. When off, every participant row is treated as a plain co-author and the submitter's contact link is never moved; when on, the form matches the self row against the submitter's profile email without changing the contact link or blocking the submit.

enable.path: Sessions → Forms → [form] → Contacts step → Enable "This is me"

entries.use_case: Organizers who experienced contact-link confusion or "vanished abstract" reports after the self-participant feature shipped can leave it off on all existing forms and opt specific forms in only when they are ready to test the behaviour.

cs_action.note: The toggle is off by default on every existing form, including any that were live during the AUA 2027 abstract deadline. No action is needed to keep the old behaviour. Only turn it on for a specific form after confirming with the organizer that they want the self-row matching logic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about the 'This is me' participant row, reports co-author email confusion, or wants to pilot the submitter-identification feature on a single form.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer running a CfP with co-author participant rows who wants to control whether the submitter's row is auto-identified.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → Forms → [form] → Contacts step → Enable "This is me"
internal.gotchas: All existing forms default to off, so the self-participant behaviour from the SB-10095 rollout is fully reverted for every form until an admin explicitly enables it. The API also strips is_self from posted participants when the flag is off, so third-party integrations posting is_self will have it silently ignored.
internal.talk_track: The 'This is me' feature is now a per-form opt-in. Your existing forms are unaffected; you can turn it on for a specific form when you're ready to try it.

draft.docs_gap: The submission-forms guide should document the Enable "This is me" toggle in the Contacts step, explain what it does when on vs. off, and note that it defaults to off on all forms.
draft.why_use_it: Submission forms let submitters list themselves alongside co-authors as session participants. The "This is me" toggle gives organizers precise control over whether the form identifies the submitter's own row, so they can enable the behaviour on forms where it has been tested and leave it off everywhere else. This prevents unintended contact-link changes and keeps the review step free of unexpected warnings for submitters on forms where the feature is not needed.

entries.title: Control whether CfP submitters can mark themselves as a session participant
entries.summary: A new **Let submitters mark themselves as a participant** switch on the form editor's **Contacts** step controls whether the **"This is me"** option appears on the public submission form. The switch is off by default, so all existing forms return to the pre-feature behaviour; turn it on per form to restore the self-participant flow, including the **"Submitting as you / Is this really you?"** callout on the review step.

enable.path: Sessions → Forms → [form] → Edit → Contacts step → Let submitters mark themselves as a participant

entries.use_case: Organizers who want submitters to be able to identify themselves as a session participant can enable the switch on the specific forms where that makes sense, while leaving it off for forms where it caused confusion or unexpected duplicate-contact tickets.

cs_action.note: The switch is off by default on every existing form. Any customer who was relying on the 'This is me' radio (enabled in a previous release) will no longer see it until they turn the switch on. Proactively check with customers who had the feature enabled and let them know they need to opt back in per form.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why the 'This is me' option disappeared from their CfP form, or when onboarding a customer who wants submitters to self-identify as participants.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer running a CfP where the submitter is also a session speaker or participant.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → Forms → [form] → Edit → Contacts step → Let submitters mark themselves as a participant
internal.gotchas: All existing forms default to off regardless of prior state. Customers who had the feature active before this change must re-enable it manually on each form.
internal.talk_track: You now control the 'This is me' self-participant option per form — turn it on only for the forms where it makes sense, and leave it off elsewhere to keep the submission flow clean.

draft.docs_gap: The submission forms guide should document the new "Let submitters mark themselves as a participant" switch on the Contacts step, including its default-off behaviour and what the review-step callout looks like when it is enabled.
draft.why_use_it: Submission forms let speakers and other contributors propose sessions directly, capturing all the participant details you need in one step. The Contacts step controls who is attached to each submission, and per-form settings let you tailor the experience to different submission tracks without creating separate events.

entries.title: Attendees can connect Claude or ChatGPT to their own event data
entries.summary: Attendees can now link their AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, or any MCP-compatible tool) to their personal event data. After an organizer enables **AI Assistants** in the event's Attend app settings, attendees generate a one-time connection code in the app and paste it into their assistant to grant read-only access to their schedule, saved sessions, moments, credits, and session recaps — scoped strictly to that event. Connections appear under **Connections** in the app and can be revoked at any time. Off-record sessions and sensitive credit links are automatically withheld from the assistant.

enable.path: Attend → Settings → AI Assistants → Enabled

entries.use_case: Attendees who use Claude or ChatGPT can ask their assistant questions like "What sessions do I have saved tomorrow?" or "Summarize the recap from the keynote" without leaving their AI tool. Organizers enable it once per event and attendees self-serve the connection.

cs_action.note: The feature is off by default per event. Organizers must turn on AI Assistants in the Attend app settings before attendees see the connection flow. Remind organizers that off-record sessions are automatically hidden from the assistant and that attendees can hold a maximum of 10 live connections.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When talking to customers who use the Attend app and whose attendees are active Claude or ChatGPT users, or during Attend app onboarding conversations.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with an active Attend app deployment where attendees are likely to use AI assistants for scheduling or content discovery.
internal.staff_path: Attend → Settings → AI Assistants (toggle Enabled); attendee flow is in the Attend mobile app under Connections.
internal.gotchas: Off by default — nothing shows in the app until the organizer enables it. Tokens expire 30 days after the event (90-day hard cap). Max 10 live connections per attendee. Off-record sessions and certificate/claim links in credits are stripped from MCP responses. Cancelling or transferring a registration immediately invalidates all tokens for that attendee.
