internal.talk_track: Attendees can ask their AI assistant about their schedule and session recaps right inside Claude or ChatGPT — no copy-paste, no switching apps. You turn it on once in Attend settings and attendees connect themselves.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a dedicated section explaining the attendee-facing MCP connector: how attendees generate a one-time connection code in the Attend app, paste it into their AI assistant, what data the assistant can and cannot access (off-record sessions, credit certificate links are withheld), and how to revoke connections.
draft.why_use_it: Connecting your AI assistant to Sessionboard lets you query your personal event schedule, saved sessions, moments, credits, and session recaps in natural language — directly inside Claude, ChatGPT, or any MCP-compatible assistant. The connection is read-only and scoped to a single event, so the assistant sees only what you have access to as a registered attendee. You can revoke access at any time from the app.

entries.title: Control whether attendees can use the event in Claude or ChatGPT
entries.summary: A new **Let attendees use this event in Claude / ChatGPT** toggle appears in the event app's **Sign-in & privacy** settings. When enabled, attendees can query event data through connected AI assistants. The switch is currently visible to super users only while it rolls out.

enable.path: Attend → App Design → Sign-in & privacy → Let attendees use this event in Claude / ChatGPT

entries.use_case: Organizers who want to let attendees explore the event schedule, sessions, and speakers through AI assistants like Claude or ChatGPT can opt in per event, keeping control over which events expose data to those tools.

cs_action.note: Switch is gated to super users only during rollout. Do not surface to customers until the gate is lifted.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about AI assistant integrations or the MCP connector for their event app.
internal.who_should_get_it: Super users / staff only for now; general availability TBD pending API rollout.
internal.staff_path: Attend → App Design → Sign-in & privacy → Let attendees use this event in Claude / ChatGPT
internal.gotchas: The toggle is hidden entirely until the web-api ships the `mcp` setting key — it will not appear in older API environments. Non-super-user admins cannot see or toggle it yet.
internal.talk_track: We are rolling out the ability for attendees to query event data through Claude and ChatGPT. Organizers will have a per-event on/off switch in the app's Sign-in & privacy settings.

draft.docs_gap: The Sign-in & privacy section of the mobile-app guide should document the new AI assistants toggle, what it enables for attendees, and how it relates to the Connect AI assistants guide.
draft.why_use_it: Connecting your event to AI assistants lets attendees ask natural-language questions — "What sessions cover machine learning?" or "When does the keynote start?" — and get instant, personalised answers without hunting through the app. You decide which events participate, so sensitive or invite-only events stay private. The integration works with the AI assistants attendees already use every day, reducing the learning curve for first-time app users.

entries.title: Co-author rows that share the submitter's email no longer overwrite the submitter's name
entries.summary: When a submitter enters their own email address on a co-author row in a Call for Papers form, the name typed on that co-author row no longer overwrites the submitter's contact record. The submitter's own name is preserved, and the co-author participant is still attached to the submission with all non-identity fields intact.
entries.use_case: Conferences that collect co-author information on their CFP forms no longer see submitters' names silently changed when a co-author row happens to carry the submitter's own email address — keeping contact records accurate across all past and future submissions.

cs_action.note: Contacts that were already renamed by this bug are not automatically corrected. CS should proactively check affected events — particularly large CFP events — and offer to help customers correct contact names that were overwritten before this fix shipped.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that a speaker's or submitter's name changed unexpectedly after a CFP submission, or when reviewing AUA 2027 (event 6153) follow-ups.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running a CFP form that collects co-author or additional participant rows, especially where submitters may enter their own email on a co-author row.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → Submission Forms → (open a CFP form) → Submissions
internal.gotchas: Historical contact records that were already overwritten by this bug are not retroactively fixed by this PR. A companion PR (SSO hydration resync) addresses a related rename vector. Non-identity fields (Bio, Title, etc.) typed on the submitter's email on a co-author row still write to the submitter's contact, as before.
internal.talk_track: A bug in CFP form conversion could silently rename a submitter's contact record whenever a co-author row shared the submitter's email. That is now fixed — the submitter's name is always preserved, and the co-author is still attached to the submission.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that when a co-author row on a CFP form shares the submitter's email address, only the submitter's own row updates their name and email — co-author rows on the same email address update other fields but do not overwrite the submitter's identity.
draft.why_use_it: null

entries.title: App connections are named automatically when you add them
entries.summary: When adding a new app connection, Sessionboard now generates a name automatically — using the connected account name (e.g. the Slack workspace or portal domain) when available, or the app name with a numeric suffix to avoid duplicates (e.g. **LinkedIn Events**, **LinkedIn Events 2**). You can rename a connection at any time; renaming it clears the auto-generated flag so the name is preserved even if the connected account changes.

where.path: Apps → App Marketplace → [any app] → Add connection

entries.use_case: Organizers who connect multiple accounts of the same app (e.g. two Slack workspaces or several portals) no longer need to type a name on creation — each connection gets a meaningful, unique name immediately and can be renamed afterwards to match internal conventions.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer manages multiple connections for the same app and has complained about naming friction or confusion in the connections list.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer who connects more than one account of the same app.
internal.staff_path: Apps → App Marketplace → [any app] → connections list
internal.gotchas: Legacy rows that predate this change still fall back to the app's default name in the list; they are not retroactively renamed. OAuth-connected apps (e.g. Slack) and Luma will update the auto-generated name to match the connected account after OAuth completes, but a name the admin typed manually is always preserved.
internal.talk_track: Adding a second Slack workspace or a second portal connection no longer asks for a name — Sessionboard picks one from the account and deduplicates it, so the list stays readable without any extra steps.

draft.docs_gap: The App Marketplace guide should note that connection names are generated automatically on creation and can be renamed from the connection's edit screen.
draft.why_use_it: The App Marketplace lets you connect third-party platforms — registration systems, event apps, webinar tools and more — so data flows between Sessionboard and the tools your team already uses. When you manage several connections for the same app, clear names make it easy to tell them apart and map the right connection to the right event.

entries.title: Adding an app connection no longer asks for a name
entries.summary: The **Add a connection** form no longer shows a **Name** field. Connections are named automatically after the app or the connected account. To rename a connection, use **Edit connection**, which keeps the **Name** field; leaving it blank resets the name to the automatic value.
entries.use_case: Organizers can connect an app in fewer steps — no need to think of a name upfront. The connection is named automatically, and renaming is available any time from Edit connection.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer mentions friction when setting up integrations or asks how connections are named.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer who adds app connections.
internal.staff_path: Apps → [any app] → Add a connection
internal.gotchas: This UI change is paired with an API change (sessionboard-web-api: 'Apps: name new connections automatically') that names connections server-side. The UI is safe against the current API because displayName is already optional on create and the list falls back to the app name client-side.
internal.talk_track: Adding a connection is now one less decision — just authenticate and go. You can always rename it from Edit connection later.

draft.docs_gap: The App Marketplace guide should note that connections are named automatically on creation and can be renamed from Edit connection.
draft.why_use_it: The App Marketplace lets you connect Sessionboard to your registration platform, event app, webinar tool, and other services. Connections are set up once and keep your sessions, speakers, and contacts in sync across systems without manual exports.
